review_method: direct pixel inspection at thumbnail and native scale

gates.visible_evidence: The frame contains one woman and one clearly adult male counterpart. Her rightward gaze, turned face, angled upper body, extended arm, and canister-transfer axis all terminate at that same man.
gates.substitute_confusion: Her pupils do not address the lens, and no second person competes for the gaze, body orientation, offered object, or response.

gates.visible_evidence: At native scale both alert pupils and her chin point right toward the man's face; her right shoulder advances, the left shoulder recedes, and the chest-and-torso plane turns three-quarter toward him along the reaching arm.
gates.substitute_confusion: This is not an arm-only cue: shoulder depth and the blazer-and-blouse torso plane visibly turn with the head, unlike the substantially camera-frontal torso in attempt 02.

gates.visible_evidence: At the open brass booth threshold she holds a silver film canister in midair toward the man across the deliberately clear upper span of the luggage trolley.
gates.substitute_confusion: The canister is visibly supported by her outstretched hand and projected across their shared space, rather than serving as a passive prop on the trolley.

gates.visible_evidence: At thumbnail scale the man is stopped opposite the threshold and his open right hand reaches into the gap directly under and toward the offered canister.
gates.substitute_confusion: The receiving hand remains legible without facial detail, so the frame is not merely a static two-person portrait or a direct-gaze substitute.

repair_delta_observed: Relative to attempt 02, the woman's upper torso and shoulder depth rotate toward the man while the same counterpart, offered canister, open threshold, clear trolley span, and his reaching hand remain visible.
audit_boundary: The judgments above come from inspected pixels. Prompt and request-audit presence was not counted as pixel evidence.
